newsitem.title: USA: ITT in definitive deal to sell Madison Square Garden.
newsitem.headline: ITT in definitive deal to sell Madison Square Garden.

text.p: ITT Corp. said Wednesday it has signed a definitive agreement to sell its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden to its partner, Cablevision Systems Corp., for $650 million, and said it will also throw in one of its aircraft to sweeten the deal.

The two companies reached an agreement in principle last month, and the transaction is expected to be completed in June. ITT has been selling assets to thwart a hostile $6.5 billion takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp.
Hilton launched its bid in late January, and ITT subsequently rejected it as inadequate.
In recent weeks, Hilton sent letters to ITT institutional shareholders and financial analysts questioning the sale because the ITT and Cablevision had only reached a preliminary agreement.
The definitive deal will give Cablevision control of the New York Rangers National Hockey League team and the New York Knicks basketball team, as well as the MSG television network.
In addition to the previous agreement, ITT has agreed to contribute one of its aircraft, which MSG has used for the Knicks and Rangers sports teams.
To pay for the aircraft, Cablevision will add an additional $19 million to each of two previously announced $75 million purchase options contained in the agreement.
Meanwhile, ITT and Hilton prepared for a Thursday hearing in United States District Court in Las Vegas concerning Hilton's motion to compel ITT into holding its annual meeting in mid-May.

Hilton has nominated a slate of directors to unseat ITT's current board at ITT's the meeting, which has traditionally been held in mid-May but could take place as late as mid-November. ITT has yet to schedule the meeting.

In court documents Hilton has asked the judge to force the meeting next month. Hilton argues that ITT's bylaws and Nevada state law require an annual meeting within one year from the previous meeting date.

ITT claims its bylaws and state law do not require a mid-May meeting. Indeed, it claims it has 18 months from the previous year's date to hold its annual meeting, which means it could hold the meeting as late as November.
